messages:
alex: quick sanity check — I'm hitting 401 on streaming with the Node SDK when the API key comes from an env var on macOS. code I'm using:

alex: ```
const apiKey = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
const auth = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:`).toString('base64')
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: auth } })
```

alex: works locally if I hardcode the key, but fails when reading from my clipboard / env. anyone seen something like this?

priya: check for a trailing newline — pbpaste/pbcopy and some editors add one. do: `console.log(JSON.stringify(apiKey))` or `console.log(apiKey.length)` to confirm.

mike: also GH Actions/GCP secret uploads sometimes add a newline if pasted with a trailing return. quick fix: `const clean = apiKey && apiKey.trim()` or `Buffer.from(apiKey.trim() + ':')` when building the header.

sophie: streaming endpoints are picky — if the header doesn't exactly match the registered key you get 401s with no extra info. verify the header sent with a local `curl -v` using the base64 string.

alex: ran `JSON.stringify(apiKey)` — showed a `"\n"` at the end. `.trim()` fixed the 401. thanks. I'll update how I store the secret.

alex: fyi I added a tiny helper in my app while debugging: `function authHeaderFromEnv(k){ if(!k) return null; return 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(k.trim() + ':').toString('base64') }`

priya: note: don't do global `replace(/\\s+/g, '')` — that could remove internal spaces if a key legitimately has them. `trim()` is safer.

mike: opened a micro PR to the SDK to add a dev-only warning when an env key length differs from the expected length; put @sophie as reviewer.

ci-bot: PR #1234 opened: devex/sdk#1234 — added env-key trim dev warning (CI checks passed).

alex: :thumbsup: good call. saving this in the troubleshooting docs and moving on.

sophie: also added a one-liner to our docs: "If you paste an API key on macOS, run `pbpaste | tr -d '\\n' | pbcopy` to strip newline before saving to secret stores."

alex: thanks all — closing this quick thread.
